note: Operator cheat sheets for the stages a command builder does not cover: what to check after you land a shell, and how to move files. Privilege-escalation abuses are from GTFOBins. Nothing runs; the page hands you text.

sections.name: Enumerate first
sections.intro: Run these before anything else. Most escalations are visible in the output.

items.note: Who you are, and what you may run as root without a password. Check sudo -l first, always.
Every SUID binary. Cross-check each against GTFOBins.
SGID binaries, the same idea for group privilege.
File capabilities. cap_setuid on a binary is root.
Scheduled jobs. A writable script run by root is a clean escalation.
Kernel and distro version, for a kernel exploit as a last resort.

sections.name: SUID and sudo abuse (GTFOBins)
sections.intro: If one of these is SUID or in your sudo -l, it is a root shell.
sections.warn: These escalate privilege. Only on a system you are authorized to test, and record each one used.

items.note: find via sudo spawns a shell as the target user.
find as a SUID binary: -p keeps the elevated euid.
vim via sudo drops to a shell.
awk via sudo runs a shell from BEGIN.
Old nmap (<5.21) with --interactive has !sh.
env runs any binary; via sudo that is a root shell.
Hard-coded credentials in config.
Commands others typed, sometimes with passwords inline.
Writable passwd or readable shadow is immediate escalation.
Writable directories, for a cron or PATH hijack.

If both HKLM and HKCU are 1, any MSI runs as SYSTEM.
Credentials in config files, unattend.xml, web.config.
Stored credentials you can reuse with runas /savecred.
